output: Manchester City captain Vincent Kompany criticizes UEFA’s Financial Fair Play (FFP) regulations, arguing they protect established clubs rather than fostering competition. Kompany believes FFP hinders newer or smaller clubs from competing against well-established teams financially, citing Manchester City's success under Sheikh Mansour's ownership as an example of how significant investments can lead to a club's growth and community benefits. He contends that FFP rules prevent emerging teams from challenging the traditional elite, thus maintaining the status quo.

England Sevens international Jeff Williams has signed with Bath for the upcoming season, bringing with him valuable experience from the World Series circuit where he has scored 36 tries. Bath's head coach, Mike Ford, is excited about Williams' dynamic playing style and his fit with the team's attacking approach, while also praising his physical presence that will complement their game. Williams, who previously played in South Africa and France, will now have the opportunity to transition to 15-a-side rugby and compete at the highest level in the Aviva Premiership.

Director David Ayer revealed the first full look at Jared Leto portraying the Joker in "Suicide Squad," a film set to be released in 2016 without the presence of Batman. Leto transformed for the role by cutting his hair and shaving his face, marking him as the first actor to play the iconic character since Heath Ledger. The film, which also features Will Smith, Margot Robbie, and other villains and anti-heroes, is scheduled for release on August 5, 2016.

Three Florida corrections officers, including a former trainee, plotted to murder a former inmate who was scheduled to be released from prison, according to charges filed by the Florida Attorney General's office. The plot was uncovered when an FBI informant, who had infiltrated a KKK branch, met the officers, and they expressed their desire for the inmate's death. The officers were led to believe the crime was successful through a staged fake homicide scene orchestrated by the FBI.

The conference call for Manny Pacquiao's pre-fight media event was abruptly cancelled due to technical difficulties, affecting over 100 participants including boxing writers and broadcasters. During the brief call, Pacquiao managed to answer only one question about his training, to which he responded positively. The call was rescheduled as an apology was issued by the promoters.

Serena Williams received a large cake to celebrate her 700th career victory at the Miami Open, following her victory over Sabine Lisicki. Meanwhile, Andy Murray also celebrated his 500th win with a cake presentation. Despite the cake celebrations, Williams was unable to meet her sister Venus in the semi-finals as Venus was defeated by Carla Suarez Navarro.

Beijing International Airport is constructing the world's largest terminal, Terminal 1, to accommodate the growing number of Chinese tourists traveling internationally. Designed by Zaha Hadid, this six-tier structure will span 700,000 square meters and cater to 45 million passengers annually, aiming to enhance connectivity and reduce walking distances through innovative architectural design. This terminal reflects China's rapid expansion in international tourism, with outbound travelers increasing from 10 million in 2000 to 109 million by 2014, contributing $164 billion to the global economy.

Manchester United's manager, Louis van Gaal, reported that Wayne Rooney suffered a knee injury during Manchester United's 3-0 loss to Everton, though the severity is still unknown. This setback follows back-to-back league defeats under Van Gaal’s management, which has now allowed Liverpool to close the gap in the race for Champions League qualification. The injury occurred in the closing stages of the match, with Rooney being substituted and seen receiving treatment.

Manchester City is reportedly considering signing Jack Wilshere, who was recently seen showing off his extensive shopping trip on Instagram. During his day off, the Arsenal midfielder shared photos of his grocery haul, which included various cereals, eggs, baked beans, and corn on the cob, aimed at aiding his recovery from ankle surgery. Wilshere humorously sought help from his followers to assist with unloading his heavily stocked trolley.

A Venezuelan woman named Marleni Olivo threw a handwritten note on a mango at President Nicolas Maduro during a rally, an act that gained viral attention. In response, Maduro granted Olivo an apartment as part of his housing mission, fulfilling her long-standing wish. The incident sparked criticism from Maduro’s opponents but was seen as a humorous and unconventional interaction between a citizen and the president.

Carlos Tevez, a former Manchester United and City striker, believes it is more challenging to score goals in Serie A compared to the Premier League. He attributes this difference to the more robust defensive presence and less dynamic midfield play in Serie A, despite having scored 36 goals for Juventus since 2013. Tevez also expresses confidence in Juventus's ability to achieve success, including potentially winning the Champions League, comparing their current team to the one that won the title in 2008.

Jamie Carragher accused Yaya Toure of ducking out of the way of Jason Puncheon's free-kick during a Premier League match between Manchester City and Crystal Palace, suggesting this was unacceptable behavior from a high-paid player. The incident occurred as a five-man wall was set up, with Toure appearing to avoid the ball while others positioned themselves to block it, potentially costing City valuable points. This criticism followed a 2-1 loss that left City nine points behind leaders Chelsea.

A 50-year-old Australian man died suddenly after collapsing at a hotel restaurant in Kuta, Bali, with reports suggesting he suffered a heart attack. The man, from Seymour in Victoria, was staying at the 101 Legian Hotel when he fell ill; an autopsy is pending to confirm the cause of death. Kuta, known for its beaches and popularity among Australian tourists, remains a major tourist destination despite the tragic incident.

Former Australian cricket captain and commentator Richie Benaud was honored with a private funeral service in Sydney, attended by close family, friends, and former teammates, after declining a state funeral offered by the Australian Prime Minister. Benaud, known for both his playing career and extensive work as a commentator, passed away at the age of 84 due to complications from skin cancer. The cricket world paid tribute to him through various memorials and tributes, recognizing his significant impact on the sport.

Isobel Attwood, a 16-year-old schoolgirl from Winchester, Hampshire, has been missing for two days and is believed to be with a man in his 20s in Southampton, according to friends who posted on social media. Police are concerned for her welfare and believe she could be in the Winchester or Southampton areas, though they have not been able to locate her despite several lines of inquiry. Officers are urging Isobel to contact them if she is reading this, emphasizing that she is not in trouble and needs to return home safely.

If Manchester City fail to qualify for the Champions League this season, key players like Sergio Aguero, David Silva, Joe Hart, and Yaya Touré could lose up to £500,000 each in bonuses. The team faces a critical challenge, currently sitting in fourth place, with Liverpool only four points behind them after City's recent loss to Manchester United. The stakes are high, with nearly £12 million in bonuses dependent on securing a top-four finish to directly qualify for the Champions League.

Martin Skrtel, a Liverpool defender, has dismissed rumors linking him with moves to Wolfsburg or Napoli, stating he plans to remain with Liverpool despite his contract expiring in 2016. His agent confirms that the only offer on the table is an extension to his contract, and denies any interest from Wolfsburg. Liverpool, having had a disappointing season, is expected to undergo a clear-out in the summer, though Skrtel is committed to staying with the team.

Cheryl Rios, a female CEO from Texas, sparked controversy by claiming that women should not be president due to their "hormones," which she believes would prevent them from starting wars. Her comments were met with widespread criticism and accusations of misogyny, particularly on social media. Despite defending her right to express her opinions, Rios maintained that she supports women in other professions while reiterating her belief that they are unsuitable for the presidency.

Mario Mandzukic, despite suffering injuries in the Champions League quarter-final first leg against Real Madrid, is expected to be fit for the return match at the Bernabeu on Wednesday, according to Atletico Madrid's coach Diego Simeone. Simeone believes Mandzukic will be ready to play after a series of training sessions, though the striker showed visible signs of the physical confrontation. Additionally, Simeone expressed optimism about Mandzukic's attacking partner Antoine Griezmann, praising his recent form and potential.

Chelsea's Jose Mourinho prepared his team to face Marouane Fellaini, only to learn from a hotel doorman that the Manchester United player was not going to be in the match. The doorman explained that Fellaini was actually there to pick up tickets for Eden Hazard and turned out to be Fellaini's twin brother, Mansour. Despite the misunderstanding, Chelsea won the game 1-0 and moved closer to winning the Premier League title.

Dawn Milosky, a 45-year-old woman from Beachwood, New Jersey, was involved in a serious accident where her 2006 Toyota Solara convertible overturned and caught fire. Police responding to a tip about erratic driving rescued Milosky, who had been knocked unconscious, just as the car began to burn; she required emergency medical attention including defibrillation and CPR. Milosky has been charged with driving while intoxicated, reckless driving, and other related offenses.

A farmer in eastern China has found himself in the spotlight after one of his goats gave birth to a six-legged kid, dubbed a "spider goat" by Chinese internet users. The baby goat, born 20 days ago, initially had four forelegs and two hind legs but as it grew, two of the forelegs became shorter and cannot touch the ground. The farmer, Xiao Qibin, plans to let the unique goat grow naturally without attempting to remove the extra legs.

West Ham United is considering signing Javier Hernández from Real Madrid as part of their summer recruitment plan. The 26-year-old striker, known as "Little Pea," is set to return to Manchester United at the end of the season and could be available for around £7 million. Alongside this, West Ham is also targeting young players such as Pedro Obiang, Moussa Konate, and Fabian Schar.

Stuart McCall, the manager of Rangers, has dismissed any speculation about his future with the club before the end of the season, emphasizing that the team's recent success has yet to translate into tangible achievements. McCall arrived at Rangers on a short-term deal aimed at reviving their promotion push and has restored a positive atmosphere within the club. Despite the team's recent winning streak and improved morale, McCall insists that no meaningful discussions about his contract will take place until after the play-offs.

Werder Bremen secured a narrow 1-0 victory over Hamburg SV in a crucial match, thanks to a late penalty by Franco Di Santo, keeping Bremen's hopes for a Europa League spot alive. Hamburg's Valon Behrami was sent off after bringing down Zlatko Junuzovic, and new coach Bruno Labbadia suffered a loss on his return to the club. With this win, Werder Bremen climbed to seventh place with 38 points, while Hamburg remained at the bottom with 25 points.

A two-year-old boy fell into a cheetah exhibit at the Cleveland Metroparks Zoo after slipping between a 10 to 12-foot gap while being held by his parents, who managed to rescue him before emergency services arrived. The child suffered minor injuries and was released from the hospital in stable condition. The zoo plans to press child endangerment charges against the parents, as the incident appears to have been caused by the parents dangling the child over the railing.

Russian TV channel TV Rain gave Hillary Clinton's campaign video a mature audience rating due to concerns it might violate Russia's anti-gay propaganda law, which bans the promotion of non-traditional sexual relationships to minors. The video featured a brief scene of a gay couple holding hands, leading the channel to mark it as 18+ to avoid potential legal issues. This decision reflects the uncertainty surrounding the interpretation of the law and the channel's cautious approach to avoid scrutiny from authorities.

Siem de Jong, Newcastle's 26-year-old midfielder who returned from a collapsed lung, made a comeback appearance playing 45 minutes for the Under 21s in a 2-0 loss to Derby County. Despite showing signs of fitness, de Jong's performance was described as subdued, suggesting he may not be ready for the upcoming match against Tottenham. Additionally, Newcastle's loan signing Facundo Ferreyra also came off the bench during de Jong's half of play, though he has yet to make his senior debut due to persistent injuries.

Chef Ally Lees from Alfie Bird's restaurant in Birmingham created a massive omelette weighing 12,000 calories and measuring three feet in circumference as a special Easter promotion. The enormous dish, made with 150 eggs, is so large that it requires at least five people to finish it, and it contains 16 times the recommended daily protein intake for a man.

Three Olympic gold medalists from the 2012 London Games—Jessica Ennis-Hill, Mo Farah, and Greg Rutherford—will participate in the Sainsbury’s Anniversary Games at the Olympic Stadium. The event, which features a two-day Diamond League meeting and the IPC Athletics Grand Prix Final, is set to attract top international athletes and recreate the excitement of the 2012 Olympics. Ticket sales have begun and the event is expected to draw large crowds to the Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park from July 24-26.

Police in Rio de Janeiro uncovered a disturbing case where a snack bar was using the meat of stray dogs to make pastries, specifically 'pastels,' which are traditionally made with ground beef. The owner, a Chinese man named Van Ruilonc, admitted to using the meat of strays he had gathered from the streets. This discovery came alongside the investigation into alleged human trafficking and forced labor conditions for Chinese workers in the area.

Ebony Dickens, a resident of East Point, Georgia, posted a threatening message on Facebook under a fake name, calling for black people to kill white police officers, which led to her arrest by local and federal law enforcement agencies. The post, which detailed plans to kill multiple white cops, garnered significant attention and prompted a thorough investigation. Upon identifying Dickens, authorities found a firearm and several computers at her home during a subsequent search warrant.

PSV Eindhoven won the Dutch Eredivisie championship for the first time in seven seasons by defeating Heerenveen 4-1, securing 79 points and leaving second-place Ajax behind. Key scorers included Luuk de Jong with two headers and Memphis Depay with a stunning free kick. Meanwhile, bottom team Dordrecht suffered a 3-0 loss, putting them closer to relegation.

An 11-year-old boy named Shiva was reportedly beaten to death by his head teacher, Lalit Verma, at Dwarika Prasad School in Railamau village, India, after being accused of stealing a pencil and eraser. The teacher allegedly launched into a violent assault on Shiva, leading to his death due to internal bleeding, with the teacher himself admitting to slapping Shiva during questioning. This incident has reignited concerns over the use of extreme corporal punishment by teachers in India, as similar cases have been reported in other parts of the country.

A gastrointestinal illness affecting 100 passengers and five crew members has been reported on the Celebrity Infinity cruise ship, out of a total of 2,117 passengers and 964 crew members. The Centers for Disease Control is investigating the cause, while the ship is currently en route to San Diego where two CDC staff will conduct further tests. This is the third such outbreak on the Celebrity Infinity, with previous incidents occurring in 2006 and 2013.

A Boston Terrier named Gizmo, filmed by his owner Loren Mathieson, was seen performing an unusual walking technique after trying on new booties, lifting his hind legs in a series of vertical jumps while moving forward. The amusing video, capturing Gizmo's acrobatic movements, went viral with over 80,000 views and left many viewers smiling. Gizmo reportedly executed this trick because he was unsure how to walk in his new black boots.

New Orleans has implemented a city-wide smoking ban, which took effect on Wednesday, prohibiting smoking in most indoor public places such as bars, casinos, and restaurants. Despite initial concerns from bar owners about potential revenue loss and objections from some smokers, the ban was passed unanimously by the city council in January. The ban is part of an effort to protect workers' health and comes just before major events like Mardi Gras and jazz festivals.

Manchester United secured a crucial victory over West Ham United in the Under 21 Premier League, moving four points clear at the top of the table. Despite taking an early lead through Reece Oxford, West Ham found themselves levelled within 12 minutes thanks to goals from Josh Harrop and Joe Rothwell, with Adnan Januzaj leading the Manchester United team. The match ended 3-1 to Manchester United, with Harrop scoring the winning goal in the process.

The Anglican Archbishop of Brisbane, Phillip Aspinall, has joined a call to abolish Queensland's 'gay panic' defense, which can reduce murder charges to manslaughter if the defendant claims they felt threatened by a sexual advance. Aspinall supported this move and also addressed instances of violence at anti-Islam rallies and church vandalism, urging people to resist reacting out of fear. During his Easter Sunday mass, Aspinall emphasized the importance of embracing forgiveness and the spirit of resurrection in daily life.

Sandra Bullock has been named the world's most beautiful woman by People magazine for 2015, marking her as the oldest recipient of the honor in its history. In the accompanying cover story, Bullock reflects on her home life and emphasizes the importance of being a good person and mother over physical appearance. Despite her success in Hollywood, she maintains a humble perspective on beauty, defining it as quiet confidence and happiness rather than youth or perfection.

An improvised bomb explosion near a U.N. vehicle in Garowe, Somalia, killed six people, including four UNICEF aid workers, according to authorities. The attack, claimed by Al-Shabaab, occurred as the vehicle transported workers from their guest house to their office. In response, Somalia's President denounced the attack as an assault on the country's future and condemned it strongly.

Gary Saurage, the manager of Gator Country wildlife park in Beaumont, Texas, was called to capture a 400-pound, 11-foot-long alligator from a family's backyard pond using only his hands. The alligator, which was particularly aggressive, required significant effort to be removed and was later identified as a 35- to 40-year-old male. The incident highlights the need for residents to maintain proper barriers and not feed the alligators, as these animals can move quickly on land and pose a threat when provoked.

In recent clashes in eastern Turkey, five members of the Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) were killed and one wounded, while four Turkish soldiers were injured. In response, Turkish Prime Minister Ahmet Davutoglu and President Recep Tayyip Erdogan condemned the violence. This incident comes amid calls from the imprisoned PKK leader Abdullah Ocalan for an end to the conflict and a peaceful resolution process with the Turkish government.

Two 18-month-old twin boys tragically died after falling into a canal in Yuma, Arizona, on Friday morning. After a search lasting over an hour, the children were found and airlifted to a local hospital, where they were pronounced dead. No suspicious activity was reported, and the incident appears to be an accidental fall while the family was out for a walk.

Orlando City, a Major League Soccer team coached by Adrian Heath, has shown interest in acquiring Javier Hernández from Manchester United, potentially capitalizing on his popularity among Latin American fans. Meanwhile, several European clubs, including eight from the Premier League and others like Wolfsburg, AC Milan, and Lazio, are also vying for Hernández's services, despite United being open to selling for around £8 million. Additionally, Manchester United has offered a new contract to young midfielder Andreas Pereira, whose father has received interest from clubs such as Paris Saint-Germain, Juventus, PSV Eindhoven, and Feyenoord, as Pereira himself has yet to accept United's initial offer.

Joel Burger, 24, proposed to his girlfriend Ashley King, also 23, leading to plans for a Burger King-themed wedding. The couple, who have known each other since kindergarten, intend to serve drinks in personalized Burger King cups for guests. They met as young children when a motivational speaker coined their names as "Burger King."

A secret police intelligence report from 1964 revealed that a hit band from the 1960s and the disgraced BBC DJ Jimmy Savile both frequented a notorious pedophile brothel in Battersea, South West London. This connection was discovered through a document detailing the activities of a flat used by pedophiles. In 2013, Detective Superintendent David Grey began investigating the link after a woman came forward in 2003 alleging that Savile had sexually abused her in the 1970s following his appearances on Top of the Pops.

Sadie, a German Shepherd from Alberta, Canada, has been filmed using her nose to turn on an electric organ and then playing it with her paws, sitting on a piano stool. Despite her owner suggesting she may have made a mistake, Sadie persists with her performance until she decides to take a break after about 20 seconds. The video of Sadie playing the piano has been viewed over 12,000 times and has received positive feedback from many viewers.

A phone thief named Ivan Balashov took a selfie in a Russian shop while trying to steal a smartphone he preferred, but was caught when police recognized him from the photo. After being stopped by shop security and attempting to flee, Balashov was later identified and arrested by the police who used the selfie as evidence. He received a three-month suspended sentence for his crime.

A documentary trailer for "Amy: The Girl Behind the Name" has been released, showcasing early footage of Amy Winehouse discussing her musical journey. The film aims to provide a comprehensive look at both the musical talent and the personal struggles of the late British singer, who died at 27 due to alcohol poisoning. The documentary is set for a UK release on July 3rd and promises to include extensive unseen archive footage and previously unheard tracks, with the backing of Winehouse's family.

The article highlights several TV shows recommended for viewers to watch, including "The Big Bang Theory," where Christine Baranski and Laurie Metcalf return as the moms of Leonard and Sheldon. It also mentions "Saturday Night Live" hosting Scarlett Johansson, "Mom" with its Emmy-worthy performances by Allison Janney, and "Younger" which has been picked up for a second season. Additionally, it covers the finales of "Backstrom," "Blue Bloods," and provides a summary of the current season of "Younger."

Dame Maggie Smith's character, Violet, Countess of Grantham, may return in a new American show called "The Gilded Age," which is set in 19th-century New York and focuses on the wealthy elite. Julian Fellowes, the creator of Downton Abbey, has hinted that other familiar faces like Robert and Cora, the Earl and Countess of Grantham, might also appear as children or young adults. NBC is excited about the project, with plans to start production soon, potentially airing as early as September.

Steven Gerrard, the 34-year-old Liverpool captain, is set to start in the FA Cup semi-final against Aston Villa at Wembley Stadium, aiming to secure a trophy and end his illustrious career with a victory. This match comes after Gerrard served a three-match ban and has been used sparingly this season, but manager Brendan Rodgers trusts him to perform in such a significant game. Gerrard has not won the FA Cup since 2006 and has only played 35 times at Wembley, making this match particularly special for both his career and Liverpool's history.

A new Dr. Seuss book, "What Pet Should I Get?", has generated significant interest, leading to an increased first printing from 500,000 to 1 million copies to meet demand. This marks the first new original Dr. Seuss book since 1990 and features characters from his beloved "One Fish Two Fish Red Fish Blue Fish." The manuscript was discovered in 1991 by Audrey Geisel, Ted's widow, and re-discovered in 2013, with plans to release more books from the same collection.

Jessica Carey traveled over three hours to surprise her grandmother, Patty Lawing, with a tattoo of her from childhood. The tattoo, drawn by Jessica's husband and based on a photo of Patty when she was young, was a stunningly accurate depiction of Patty as a young woman with long red hair and dressed in a smart blouse and jacket. Patty's emotional reaction was caught on camera, where she was overwhelmed and began to cry, eliciting exclamations of beauty and shock from those around her.

At 65 years old, Annegret Raunigk, a German primary school teacher, is expecting quadruplets through fertility treatment, making her the oldest known woman to carry and deliver quadruplets. Her previous record-breaking birth of a daughter at age 55, also the oldest known case, garnered significant media attention. Raunigk's pregnancy, now in its 21st week, carries heightened medical scrutiny due to her advanced age and the complexity of a quadruplet pregnancy.

Japan's space agency, JAXA, plans to send an unmanned rover to the moon by 2018, aiming to develop soft-landing technologies potentially useful for future missions to the moon or Mars. The mission, which could cost between $83.4 million and $125 million, will involve using face recognition technology adapted from digital cameras to help the rover navigate craters. This endeavor positions Japan as a competitive player in space exploration, particularly in response to advancements made by China and India.

Dengue fever has led to an outbreak in Brazil, affecting several top football clubs and forcing key players to miss matches. Notable cases include Corinthians striker Paolo Guerrero, who is hospitalized, and Palmeiras reserve goalkeeper Aranha, both of whom will miss crucial games. In response, clubs have taken measures such as using insect repellent and checking facilities for mosquito breeding sites to protect their players.

Manchester United striker James Wilson expressed his admiration for Wayne Rooney, Robin van Persie, and Radamel Falcao, stating that he would most like to adopt Rooney's ability to take accurate free-kicks. Wilson highlighted that Rooney practices his free-kick technique daily, often hitting the target. Additionally, Wilson praised van Persie's movement and Falcao's predatory instincts within the penalty area, indicating that he aims to improve his positioning and decision-making in the box.

Archie Brown Jr., a 39-year-old father of four, was fatally shot after striking and killing a 2-year-old child who ran in front of his van in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. At the scene, another individual shot Brown and a 15-year-old boy, both of whom later died. The shooting may have been in retaliation for the child's death, according to a local alderman, though police are still investigating.

A young boy from Memphis, Tennessee, with a surprisingly mature appearance, has gained over 3,000 Twitter followers by posting pictures of gang-related activities, including posing with guns and drugs, and making sexually explicit and confrontational comments. His posts have sparked criticism from the public, with some expressing concern for his well-being and others calling for him to focus on education instead. Despite the backlash, the boy has defended himself against the criticism, claiming his tough circumstances justify his actions.

Former Redgum frontman John Schumann criticized anti-Islam protesters for using his song "I Was Only 19" at Reclaim Australia rallies, which aimed to oppose sharia law and Islamization. Schumann stated that his song promotes compassion and tolerance and should not be used to advance ignorance and intolerance. The rallies across Australia erupted into violence, resulting in multiple arrests and minor injuries, while political leaders condemned the violence and addressed the misinformation spread during the events.

Emmanuel Adebayor, a forward for Tottenham Hotspur, has tweeted that he intends to stay with the club and fight for a place in the team, despite reports suggesting he may leave. The 31-year-old Togo international has expressed his appreciation for playing in the Premier League, which he considers the best league in the world. Despite his initial success and the subsequent signing of young talent Harry Kane, Adebayor's recent form has been criticized, leading to speculation about his future at the club.

Stuart Pearce advocates for giving Manchester City's manager, Manuel Pellegrini, more time to improve the team's performance despite their recent struggles. Pearce attributes the team's decline partly to the fading influence of Yaya Toure and suggests that the squad needs significant refreshing in the upcoming summer transfer window. Despite the team's poor form, particularly highlighted by their loss to Manchester United, Pearce hopes Pellegrini remains in his position, believing he understands the need for a new approach to the team.

Steve Bruce remains optimistic about keeping Hull City in the Barclays Premier League despite a 2-0 defeat by Southampton and the team's current struggle to avoid relegation. Bruce attributes the team's difficulties to several long-term injuries to key players and expresses confidence that positive results in their remaining matches could secure their place in the league. Despite their recent setbacks, Bruce maintains that Hull City still has the potential to overcome their challenges and stay in the Premier League.

A full-scale terror alert was triggered in Reading when a passer-by reported seeing a barge on the Thames with a fake missile launcher and a dummy in a balaclava nearby. Thames Valley Police and an Army bomb disposal team were called to the scene but found the weapon to be purely ornamental. Local residents expressed disappointment and concern over the prank, deeming it reckless and inappropriate given the recent terrorist threats.

Tiger Woods suffered an unusual injury during his play at the Masters when his club hit a tree root, causing him pain and forcing him to drop his club. Despite the setback, Woods managed to finish the tournament at 5-under-par, his best result in over a year. He attributed the injury to a popped ligament in his right wrist, which he was able to pop back into place, though it remained sore.

Iker Casillas asserts he will remain at Real Madrid and compete for the starting goalkeeper position despite potential competition from Manchester United's David de Gea. Casillas, who has been with Real Madrid since 1996, emphasizes his commitment to fulfilling his contract and supporting the team's goal of retaining the Champions League title. He also expresses optimism about the upcoming semi-finals, viewing the four remaining teams as evenly matched contenders.

Embarrassing footage has surfaced showing a S300 missile launch in Russia that went spectacularly wrong, barely leaving the launchpad before falling back to the ground, causing a small explosion and leaving a trail of debris. This incident adds to concerns about the reliability of Russia's defense systems, especially following another failed launch that resulted in the deaths of six Russian missile technicians near Donetsk in Ukraine. The Russian defense budget has significantly increased under President Putin, yet such incidents suggest ongoing issues with the country's military technology and training.

Lancashire County Cricket Club has signed Australian all-rounder James Faulkner as their overseas player for the majority of the summer, replacing Peter Siddle. Faulkner, a key player in Australia's recent World Cup victory, will join the team after completing his commitments in the Indian Premier League. The club expresses great excitement about Faulkner's addition, praising his world-class status and potential to enhance both the team's performance and the fan experience at Emirates Old Trafford.

In 1996, Mary Kay Letourneau, a 34-year-old teacher, had an affair with her 13-year-old student, leading to her imprisonment for over seven years. Since her release in 2005, she has remarried Vili Fualaau and celebrated their 10th wedding anniversary, now parenting two teenage daughters together. The upcoming "20/20" interview will delve into how they maintain their relationship despite significant age differences and personal challenges, including Letourneau's plans to teach again and efforts to have her sex offender status lifted.

Jamie Carragher traveled to Spain during the international break to support his son James, who was playing for the Liverpool U12s in the Mediterranean International Cup in Girona. Carragher shared his experience through social media, posting a picture from the opening ceremony, and even spoke to a local TV station. The Liverpool team faced several challenges, drawing 1-1 with a local Catalan side and playing against other teams in their Group E.

Seattle-based filmmaker Gabriel Ng spent three months in Thailand, capturing breathtaking views of the country's coastlines, religious sites, and daily life through drone footage, resulting in a six-minute video that showcases the beauty of destinations like Ko Samui. The video, which has gained popularity on YouTube, features stunning shots of beaches, waterfalls, and temples, and has even drawn comparisons to professional productions. Ng, who owns a video production company, has previously used drones to film weddings and other locations, demonstrating his expertise in aerial cinematography.

Peter Moores stated that he is open to working with Michael Vaughan if he becomes England's new director of cricket, emphasizing that it is not a personal issue but rather about improving the team. Moores believes additional voices in the dressing room may not be necessary, depending on the role's specifics, and remains focused on the upcoming Test series. Despite the potential change in leadership, Moores intends to continue his coaching duties and support the emerging talent in the team.

Nottingham Forest plans to pursue a transfer for Blackburn's striker Jordan Rhodes, who is valued at £10 million, with Forest manager Dougie Freedman hoping a direct cash offer will succeed where previous attempts failed. Blackburn initially rejected Forest's March bid for Rhodes, but now expect further interest in both him and his strike partner Rudy Gestede, who recently scored 19 goals and has attracted attention from clubs including Hull, Crystal Palace, West Brom, and Southampton.

In a heartwarming scene captured in a North Carolina home, a trio of dogs—Sky the Husky, Sadie and Marshall the Springer Spaniels—put on a unique musical performance for their owner. Starting with Sadie's barking and followed by Sky's melodious howl, the dogs harmonize, with Sky even mouthing to Sadie as they playfully interact. The performance reaches a crescendo as all three dogs howl together in perfect harmony, their tails wagging enthusiastically until their owner calls for them to stop.

The "French Spiderman," Alain Robert, climbed the 1,007-foot Cayan Tower in Dubai without a safety harness, using only sticky tape and chalk for assistance, taking about an hour and a half to reach the top. Known for his daring climbs, Robert has previously faced legal troubles and injuries but has also complied with safety regulations in other climbs. This feat followed his earlier ascent of the Burj Khalifa in 2011, though he used a rope and harness on that occasion due to regulations.

An experimental cancer drug previously abandoned due to poor results has shown promise in reversing the effects of Alzheimer's disease when tested on mice. The drug, AZD0530, works by blocking a process that damages nerve connections in the brain responsible for memory storage, restoring both memory and reducing inflammation in affected mice. Researchers are now conducting human trials to assess its effectiveness in Alzheimer's patients, with the potential to offer a new treatment option for the condition.

In the run-up to the release of "Avengers: Age of Ultron," Marvel Studios revealed the appearance of the Vision, played by Paul Bettany, ending months of speculation. Simultaneously, the upcoming Netflix series "Daredevil" teased its lead character, and the cast of the upcoming "X-Men: Apocalypse" featured a new character, Angel, played by Ben Hardy. Additionally, the reboot of "Fantastic Four" confirmed the look of Jamie Bell's character, The Thing, addressing fan concerns.

Veteran referee Kenny Bayless will officiate the highly anticipated boxing match between Floyd Mayweather and Manny Pacquiao, having previously worked with both fighters in numerous bouts. Despite being widely regarded as one of the best referees in the world, some, like former opponent Oscar De La Hoya, believe Bayless's involvement gives Mayweather an advantage due to past interactions where Bayless frequently broke up clinches. The appointment has sparked debate among boxing enthusiasts regarding its potential impact on the outcome of the match.

Harry Kane's participation in the upcoming Under-21 European Championship is uncertain due to Tottenham Hotspur's scheduled post-season friendly in Malaysia. Manager Mauricio Pochettino is concerned about potential burnout for the 21-year-old striker, while the Football Association is in discussions with Tottenham about Kane's availability for the tournament. Kane is expected to accompany the team to Malaysia for friendly matches, but may miss the Under-21 European Championship to ensure adequate rest before the start of the new season.

A measles outbreak affecting over 130 people in California due to the B3 strain has been declared over by the California Department of Public Health after 42 days without new cases. The majority of those affected (70%) were unvaccinated, and the outbreak originated from visitors to Disney theme parks in December. Public health measures such as prompt case investigation, contact tracing, and increased awareness helped control the outbreak.

In San Miguel de Tucuman, Argentina, police are searching for a family of six caught on camera riding on a single motorbike, with two adults and four children aboard, including young children sitting in front without helmets. This incident follows a similar case in Junin where a family of seven was photographed doing the same, leading to widespread condemnation on social media. Authorities have appealed for information on the families involved, describing their actions as irresponsible and dangerous.

Andrea McVeigh, a 44-year-old social media manager, was seriously injured when she was struck by a cyclist while walking on the pavement in Bermondsey, London. The cyclist fled the scene, prompting McVeigh’s husband to chase him. McVeigh suffered significant facial injuries, including two three-inch gashes to her forehead, and is now facing a long recovery period and permanent scarring.

A few days after Hillary Clinton announced her candidacy for the presidency, her father's headstone, located in the Washburn Street Cemetery in Scranton, Pennsylvania, was found tipped over. The grave tendsman, Paul McGloin, noticed the headstone had fallen shortly after driving past it on Monday morning. While police suspect vandalism, they are also considering whether weather could have caused the incident.

A California woman, Beatriz Paez, was recorded by another woman as she was filming police activity with her cell phone. When Paez refused to stop, a U.S. marshal physically took the phone, smashed it with his foot, and kicked it away, leaving Paez feeling unsafe and terrified. Paez has since filed a complaint and is considering legal action against the marshal's actions, which she considers illegal as she was not interfering with any ongoing investigation or arrest.

Max, a 18.5-inch-tall corgi-Siberian husky cross, has become a favorite at the Dogs Trust in Basildon, Essex, where he was taken in as a stray. Known for his gentle, intelligent, and big-hearted nature, Max exemplifies the saying "good things come in small packages." His popularity is partly attributed to the rising trend of owning wolf-like breeds, driven by fans of shows like Game of Thrones, though this trend often leads to the abandonment of these dogs due to inadequate preparation for their specific needs.

Chilean pickpockets have emerged as the most effective thieves in central London, targeting wealthy tourists in areas such as the West End. According to undercover police reports, these gangs, often consisting of three to six individuals, operate with high precision, blending into groups that appear harmless to avoid suspicion. The police have noted a significant reduction in thefts due to their efforts, though the threat remains, with international gangs moving between major European cities to evade detection.

In a severe car accident near Southam, Warwickshire, a young driver's vehicle crashed into a wall, flipped over, and left him trapped underneath. Despite suffering head, chest, and leg injuries, the man survived the crash and remained conscious throughout the rescue operation, which took 25 minutes. Emergency services, including firefighters and the air ambulance, worked together to free him from the wreckage.

Fly-tippers have dumped an unprecedented 40 tonnes of industrial waste along the roadside in the Suffolk village of Walsham-le-Willows, prompting concerns and a significant cleanup effort. Described as the worst case of flytipping by a police officer in over 28 years, the waste, including materials from the carpet and veterinary industries, was reportedly transported using three tractors and trailers. The incident has garnered attention from local authorities, the National Farmers' Union, and the Country Land and Business Association, who are working together to combat such environmental offenses.

A man, believed to be mentally disturbed, attempted to enter a restricted area at Pearson International Airport in Toronto and refused to comply with security protocols, leading to his tasering by police. The incident was captured on video, showing the man mumble and stare ahead as he was tasered, causing him to fall to the ground after several seconds of visible trembling. Subsequently, the man was transferred to a hospital under Canada's Mental Health Act and no criminal charges were pursued.

Serbia's President Tomislav Nikolic's government jet had to turn back to Belgrade after the co-pilot accidentally spilled coffee on the instrument panel, causing the plane to begin tumbling through the air. The incident, which left advisers "thrown around the cabin," was initially blamed on engine failure but was later confirmed to be due to the co-pilot activating the emergency slats by mistake. As a result, the co-pilot had his license suspended, and the president canceled his planned meeting with Pope Francis in the Vatican.

In South Africa, over 300 suspects have been arrested in connection with violent attacks against foreigners, which have led to the displacement of thousands seeking refuge in temporary shelters. The government condemns the attacks and praises law enforcement for preventing further casualties, while also reminding citizens of the country's history of relying on African neighbors during difficult times. Despite the violence, there has been an outpouring of support from ordinary South Africans and organizations like the Gift of the Givers charity, which offers assistance to those affected.

A skier named Zach Birnie captured the harrowing experience of becoming caught in an avalanche while skiing off-piste in Revelstoke, Canada. Despite the terrifying ordeal, Birnie managed to escape, though he later described it as the best and worst case scenario simultaneously. Experts from the WSL Institute for Snow and Avalanche Research advised that fresh snow and steep terrain may have contributed to the avalanche, and recommended strategies for survival in similar situations.

On the hottest day of the year, two men in their 20s, who stripped off their tops, attempted to rob an Esso petrol station in Caterham, Surrey. They entered the manager's office in search of cash but were interrupted by staff and fled without acquiring any money, though they managed to take a staff member's mobile phone. Surrey Police released CCTV footage of the men, appealing for public assistance in identifying them.

The Lada Niva 4x4, starting at £13,395 on the road, is gaining popularity as an alternative to the now-defunct Land Rover Defender, thanks to its robust design and affordable price. Despite being a Russian brand that was once the subject of ridicule, the Niva has won fans worldwide due to its durability and distinctive appearance, even available in a compact van format for £10,590. However, while the Niva lacks luxury features, its simple design means it is easy to maintain, as evidenced by its use by then-Russian President Vladimir Putin, who reportedly upgraded his Niva with a German engine.

AIDS Healthcare Foundation, the largest provider of HIV and AIDS medical care in the U.S., is accused of a $20 million scam involving kickbacks for patient referrals to boost funding from Medicare and Medicaid across 12 states. Three former managers have filed a lawsuit alleging the company paid employees and patients $100 bonuses for referring patients with positive test results, starting in 2010 from the California headquarters and spreading to other locations. The foundation denies wrongdoing and maintains its approach is crucial for treating and identifying HIV-positive individuals.

Liz, a bearded dragon owned by Shannen Hussein in Melbourne, appears to understand and respond to human speech, nodding her head when asked if she's hungry and rewarded with a superworm treat. Liz is not the only star on Shannen's social media channels; her pet lamb Winter has also gained internet fame through various Vine videos. Shannen cares for a variety of animals including cats, birds, a snake, ducks, a llama, and turtles, all of which regularly feature on her popular social media content.

Travis Hatfield, an aspiring country singer from West Virginia, gained viral attention after posting a video of him singing a George Jones song to his uncle, Jamie Joe Cline, who has Down syndrome. The heartfelt performance, which has been viewed over 410,000 times, showcases the bond between the two and highlights their weekly musical duets. Travis, inspired by his surroundings and a lifelong love for country music, is now receiving interest from Nashville record labels and aims to release his own CD and potentially audition for The Voice.

Nik Wallenda, the daredevil descendant of the 'Flying Wallendas,' announced plans to walk untethered on a 400-foot observation wheel in Orlando, Florida, on April 29. The Orlando Eye, an attraction that will open to the public on May 4, will be moving during Wallenda's performance, offering views through its air-conditioned capsules. This stunt, while not the full circumference of the wheel, is seen as particularly challenging due to the larger size of the wheel and the absence of a safety pole.

Medhi Benatia, a central defender for Bayern Munich, is likely to miss both legs of the team's upcoming Champions League quarter-final against Porto due to a muscle injury that may keep him out for two to four weeks. This adds to Bayern Munich's already lengthy injury list, which includes key players like Bastian Schweinsteiger, David Alaba, Javi Martinez, and Tom Starke. Despite the injuries, Bayern Munich remains competitive in multiple competitions, including the Bundesliga where they lead by ten points and still have aspirations in the Champions League.

Bayern Munich defeated Porto 6-1 in the Champions League quarter-final second leg, advancing to the semi-finals and demonstrating their dominance under coach Pep Guardiola. This victory adds to their already impressive season, where they have scored 115 goals across all competitions so far. With five Bundesliga matches, a German Cup semi-final, and potential Champions League matches remaining, Bayern could potentially score up to 141 goals for the season if they maintain their current goal-scoring rate of 2.61 per game.

Fernando Torres credits Diego Simeone as the key figure behind Atletico Madrid's recent success, attributing their performances to Simeone's strategic vision and understanding of the team's strengths and weaknesses. Atletico Madrid has outperformed expectations under Simeone's leadership, achieving significant victories against Real Madrid and reaching the Champions League final last year. Torres, who has scored four goals since returning to Atletico Madrid, emphasizes that his team must maintain consistent performance due to the limited depth in their squad.

Two bodies were found among the wreckage of a light aircraft that crashed near Loch Etive in western Scotland. The plane was reported missing around 30 miles east of Oban and was en route from central Scotland to Tiree when it disappeared. Lifeboats, helicopters, and police were involved in the search efforts throughout the day.

A bus shatters the windscreen of a Boeing 777 passenger jet at Tashkent airport in Uzbekistan, causing significant damage but no known injuries. This incident, along with recent collisions involving Ryanair and British Airways, highlights the increasing frequency of such accidents at major airports globally, often resulting in delays and disruptions for passengers. These events underscore the importance of improved safety measures and better coordination among ground staff and pilots.

An off-duty Secret Service agent named Arthur Baldwin was arrested in Washington D.C. on charges of attempted burglary and destruction of property after allegedly breaking into a house at midnight. The agency revoked Baldwin's security clearance and placed him on leave, and he is scheduled to appear in court. This incident follows other recent controversies involving the Secret Service, including an investigation into high-ranking officials who were accused of entering a secure area at the White House while intoxicated.

Israel is developing a unique tunnelling detection system, designed to accurately identify underground activity without false alarms, following extensive consideration of over 700 proposals. The system, developed by Elbit Systems in collaboration with the Israeli Ministry of Defense, is expected to cost approximately £2.3 million per mile to install and will be deployed along the Gaza-Israel border. Initial tests have been successful, with further results expected soon.

A primary school in south London has banned all drinks except water during the school day to promote long-term pupil health, but this decision has sparked a parental backlash. Parents argue that the ban is too strict and that children should have the freedom to choose their own beverages, especially since many do not enjoy plain water. Despite the controversy, the school defends the policy as a means to protect students' health, aligning with similar bans implemented at other schools across the country.

Paul Smith will face undefeated boxer Andre Ward in a high-stakes fight on June 20 in Oakland, California. Smith, who previously lost attempts to challenge for the WBO belt, sees this as a significant opportunity against a top-tier opponent despite Ward's extended inactivity since November 2013. Both fighters expressed excitement and determination for the bout, with Ward emphasizing the need to perform at his best to defeat the challenging Smith.

German Chancellor Angela Merkel spent Easter on the island of Ischia in Italy, where she and her husband, chemistry professor Joachim Sauer, stayed at the five-star Miramare Spa Hotel. Despite the cool weather and lack of sunshine, Merkel reportedly took Pilates classes and enjoyed vegetarian meals while avoiding the hotel's pool area. Merkel's husband, who rarely accompanies her on public appearances, was again absent from the spotlight during this holiday.

Ander Herrera, a Manchester United midfielder, has scored several goals without looking at the ball or the goal, including a brace against Aston Villa where his eyes appeared to be shut during both goals. This unusual goal-scoring habit has raised questions about his vision, despite him being signed for their excellent kicking technique and creativity. Manager Louis van Gaal noted that Herrera should be more composed and control the ball before shooting, suggesting this issue is relatively new.

A 23-month-old girl tragically died after her father accidentally struck her with a pickup truck in the driveway of their home in North Las Vegas. The father and other family members were unaware that the toddler had wandered outside. The incident was ruled an accident, and no charges were filed.

The University of Connecticut baseball team has welcomed 5-year-old Grayson Hand, a child battling leukemia, as its newest member with the help of Team IMPACT. Grayson's involvement includes having his own locker and attending practices and games, while his sister Sophie was named an honorary cheerleader. This partnership represents a significant emotional support for the Hand family, symbolizing the collective effort needed to face the challenges of Grayson's illness.

A passenger on a London Midland train discovered excrement in a newspaper on the floor, causing severe delays and forcing the train to terminate early for cleaning. London Midland has vowed to provide CCTV footage of the suspect to the police for investigation. Similar incidents, such as a flight returning to London due to a foul odor from an overflowing toilet, highlight the ongoing issues with such acts of vandalism on public transportation.

James Rodriguez, the Colombian midfielder who transferred to Real Madrid for £60 million last summer, has become a key player for the team, helping them win 80% of their matches when he is in the lineup, according to Spanish newspaper Marca. Meanwhile, in other sports news, there is a discussion about Cristiano Ronaldo's potential suspension after receiving a yellow card for diving during a recent match, which could affect his availability for the upcoming weekend's game. Additionally, former Manchester City coach Roberto Mancini is reportedly planning significant changes at Inter Milan, aiming to strengthen the team with eight new signings from a list of 21 candidates, including some Premier League stars and players from other top European clubs.

A Florida man named Kenneth Crowder, who was believed to be under the influence of Flakka, a powerful and dangerous synthetic drug, attacked a police officer after being tased twice, during which he claimed he was God and attempted to stab the officer with a police badge. Crowder was arrested and charged with battery on a law-enforcement officer, resisting with violence, and assault with a deadly weapon on a law-enforcement officer. Flakka, similar in effects to a mix of crack cocaine and methamphetamine, has become increasingly prevalent in Florida, with over 670 incidents reported in 2014 alone.

A Russian Premier League match between Arsenal Tula and Torpedo Moscow was suspended for seven minutes on Sunday due to fighting between rival fans, with Torpedo supporters breaking down barriers and throwing seats at law enforcement officers. The incident led to harsh criticism of Torpedo, with their executive director expecting severe punishment from the league, and the club facing potential bans for their ongoing hooliganism despite previous sanctions.

High school girls in Huizhou, China, are undergoing military-style dagger drill training under the guidance of a former special forces soldier, aimed at teaching them self-defense techniques. The training, conducted by Inspector Tan, involves the use of non-harmful, retractable-blade knives and includes eight defensive movements; the girls also practice using common household items like chopsticks for defense. All female students at the 27th March Huizhou Integrated High School receive some form of self-defense training to help them recognize and handle dangerous situations.

AP McCoy, the champion jockey, is urging supporters to back his mount, Shutthefrontdoor, in the Grand National, where he aims to win a second time to end his career with a fairytale victory. Despite the long odds and his past experiences with the race, McCoy remains optimistic and dedicated to his dream. Should Shutthefrontdoor win, McCoy plans to retire immediately, ending a remarkable career that has spanned over two decades.

John Isner advanced to the Miami Open semifinals with a straight-sets victory over Kei Nishikori, becoming the first American male to reach the semis in Miami since 2011. In the other semifinal, Andy Murray will face Tomas Berdych, with an interesting dynamic as Berdych is coached by someone who previously worked with Murray. Additionally, tensions may rise during their match given past conflicts between Murray's former coaches and Berdych.

Former German football legend Franz Beckenbauer criticized Bayern Munich's performance in their Champions League loss to Porto, comparing it to players taking "sleeping pills." He specifically targeted defender Dante, saying his performance was akin to wearing "ski boots." Despite the harsh words, Beckenbauer still believes Bayern can turn things around, emphasizing the need for improvement if they hope to advance in the tournament.

A 21-year-old man named Arnold Quintero from San Antonio, Texas, has been arrested for allegedly imprisoning, beating, sexually assaulting, and burning a 13-year-old girl. The girl reported being held captive in a 'trap house,' where she was punched, forced to undress, and subjected to sexual abuse by Quintero, who also took photos during the incident. Quintero faces multiple charges including aggravated sexual assault of a child and possession with intent to deliver.

In Week 12 of the Betway Premier League, Michael van Gerwen and Gary Anderson each won and lost a game. Van Gerwen had an impressive start by defeating James Wade 7-0 and advancing to the May play-offs at the 02, but later lost to Gary Anderson. Anderson, after an initial loss to Stephen Bunting, secured a notable victory against Van Gerwen, averaging 105.94 and winning 7-5.

Jay Rutland, the husband of billionaire heiress Tamara Ecclestone, earns only £65 per week despite his wife's vast wealth. His company, Brigante Business Developments, reported earnings of just £3,378 for the year ending July 2014, down significantly from the previous year. Despite his modest income, Rutland and his wife maintain a lavish lifestyle, including a £45 million home and expensive gifts for their daughter, Sophia.

Jia Binhui, a 25-year-old man from southwest China, is using an unconventional method of lying over hot coals daily in the hope of killing off his leukemia cells, as he cannot afford traditional medical treatment. This homemade "barbecue" setup, built in his garden, is based on the belief that temperatures exceeding 42 degrees Celsius can eliminate cancer cells. Despite the desperate nature of his approach, Jia remains determined, having recently married his long-term girlfriend and continuing to use this method while planning to return to hospitals to assess his condition.

Leroy Fer, a Dutch midfielder for Queens Park Rangers, is set to return to the squad after recovering from a knee injury, potentially boosting the team's chances in their relegation battle. Manager Chris Ramsey hopes to include Fer in the squad for an upcoming match against West Ham, despite the player not yet being at full fitness. Ramsey acknowledges the risk but sees the inclusion of Fer as necessary to improve the team's prospects.

In the final kilometre of the Scheldeprijs race, Team Sky teammates Sir Bradley Wiggins and Geraint Thomas escaped a major crash that injured their teammate Elia Viviani, who had to go to the hospital for x-rays after hitting the barriers. The crash sent approximately 50 riders to the ground, causing significant disruption to the race. Despite the incident, Team Sky remains in good shape for the upcoming Paris-Roubaix race on Sunday.

Before their FA Cup semi-final match against Liverpool, Aston Villa's players received encouraging messages from fans displayed in their dressing room at Wembley Stadium. Teenage star Jack Grealish tweeted one such message, which read, "You have to put up with the rain to see the rainbow! Three seasons of rain boys, time to find the end of that rainbow and prove we're the pride of the Midlands!" Additionally, goalkeeper Brad Guzan shared that he had received a message telling the team to "fight like Lions."

A 12-year-old boy named Hanghang in central China suffered severe injuries when his old mobile phone exploded while charging, exposing parts of his jawbone and embedding fragments in his arms and legs. Doctors at Ping Mei Group Hospital are treating him and expect multiple surgeries to repair the damage. Experts suggest improper charging is the most common cause of such explosions, and recommend avoiding using the phone while charging, ensuring it is not overcharged, and replacing batteries that appear swollen.

Mike Rowe, known for his work on "Dirty Jobs," highlights Chad Pregracke, founder of Living Lands & Waters, as an example of someone who inspires positive change. Since its inception in 1998, Living Lands & Waters has engaged over 87,000 volunteers to collect 8.4 million pounds of trash from U.S. waterways, earning Pregracke multiple awards including the 2013 CNN Hero of the Year. Pregracke's mission in 2015 was to remove an additional 500,000 pounds of trash and offers opportunities for public involvement through their website.

The ancient Tuscan town of Balestrino, dating back to the 11th century, became uninhabited due to seismic instability from multiple earthquakes, including one measuring 6.7 on the Richter scale in 1887. Now considered the most famous abandoned location in Italy, the town, once home to 800 inhabitants, is shrouded in mystery and folklore suggesting it is haunted. Drone footage captures the eerie beauty of the deserted town, featuring a grand castle and decaying buildings overgrown with vegetation.

At an emotional event in Anaheim, California, the cast and director of "Star Wars: Episode VII -- The Force Awakens" premiered the movie's trailer to an enthusiastic audience, who were visibly moved by the return of Han Solo and the presence of Harrison Ford. The event also showcased new characters and locations, including the planet Jakku and a droid named BB-8, while hinting at the involvement of Luke Skywalker and Princess Leia. Additionally, director J.J. Abrams emphasized that the film would feature less CGI than the prequels, with much of the movie shot on actual sets.

Former Toronto Mayor Rob Ford announced that he will undergo surgery to remove a cancerous tumor in his abdomen, following successful chemotherapy and radiation treatments. The eight to ten-hour procedure, scheduled for May 11th, aims to shrink the tumor to a more manageable size, with Ford hoping to return to work as a city councilor in September. Ford expressed gratitude for his support system, including his family and medical team, emphasizing his optimism about the future despite the risks involved.

The University of Cape Town recently removed a statue of Cecil Rhodes, a British colonialist, after weeks of student protests under the hashtag #RhodesMustFall. The students argue that Rhodes' legacy is tainted with racism and do not want his representation at the university, aiming instead for a more Afrocentric educational environment. However, this action has sparked controversy among Afrikaner groups who see the removal as erasing history rather than engaging in meaningful dialogue about South Africa's complex past.

Michael Phelps won the 100 meters butterfly event at the Arena Pro Swim Series in Arizona, marking his return to competitive swimming after a six-month suspension due to a drink-driving conviction. The 18-time Olympic gold medalist expressed joy at being back in competition but noted that he will miss the upcoming World Championships in Kazan. Phelps remains determined to compete in the 2016 Olympics in Rio de Janeiro.

A woman was found hanging from a fire escape in Crown Heights, New York, with her body left dangling for over an hour. Neighbors were traumatized by the scene, with one witness initially believing it was a Halloween prank. The victim, described as a "very social, nice girl" by neighbors, had a history of mental health issues.

Lyon reclaimed the top spot in Ligue 1 with a 2-2 draw against Saint-Etienne in a thrilling Rhone derby, despite being down to 10 men for part of the match. Meanwhile, Lille maintained their pursuit of a top-four finish by defeating Bordeaux 2-0, keeping within four points of fourth place. Additionally, Montpellier secured a narrow 1-0 victory over Caen thanks to an early header from Brazilian defender Hilton, helping them move up to seventh place in the standings.

Arsenal manager Arsène Wenger admits he did not initially expect key players Hector Bellerin and Francis Coquelin to be contributing so significantly to the team's late push for the Premier League title. Bellerin, who had only recently returned from a loan spell at Watford, scored a crucial goal against Liverpool, while Coquelin has become a regular first-team fixture. Despite some early doubts about their abilities, Wenger praises both players for their performances and attributes their success to remaining open-minded and making the right decisions.

Fox is developing a two-hour remake of the cult classic "The Rocky Horror Picture Show" for television, set to be directed, executive-produced, and choreographed by Kenneth Ortega. Scheduled to celebrate the film's 40th anniversary, the project, tentatively titled "The Rocky Horror Picture Show Event," aims to recreate the musical on screen with few details revealed so far. This isn't the first attempt at adapting the film for television; previous plans in 2002 did not materialize, and Fox had already aired a "Glee" special featuring the show's music in 2010.

Roma FC has been ordered to close part of their stadium for their next home game due to offensive banners displayed by their supporters during a recent match against Napoli. These banners, which insulted the mother of a Napoli fan who died in violent clashes following a previous match, were deemed provocative by a Serie A disciplinary tribunal. In response, the club's president has condemned the behavior, emphasizing the need for respect and unity in light of such tragic events.

Ellen White scored a stunning goal against her former club, Arsenal, in the 26th minute of the Women's Super League match by taking advantage of a confusing free-kick situation. Despite the successful execution of the set-piece from training, White later missed a penalty opportunity that could have given Notts County a lead. Arsenal ultimately equalized late in the game, securing a draw.

Arsene Wenger acknowledges that letting Eden Hazard join Chelsea in 2012 for £32 million was a missed opportunity, despite not regretting the decision due to financial constraints at the time. Despite the regret, Wenger believes Hazard has had a standout season, scoring 18 goals and assisting 10 in 43 starts, and is considered a strong contender for the Player of the Season award. Wenger also sees his own player, Alexis Sanchez, as a serious rival in the voting, believing both players have shown significant improvement over the past few seasons.

Stephen Akers-Belcher, the Mayor of Hartlepool, was dismissed from his position as a care manager with Newcastle City Council after claiming he needed time off for a funeral but was found to have visited HMS Warrior instead, 323 miles away. The council denied he was dismissed for whistleblowing and stated that they had thoroughly investigated his allegations regarding the protection of vulnerable adults, finding no further action necessary. Akers-Belcher maintained his innocence, stating he had done nothing wrong.

Dr. John Parker, a humanitarian doctor who had been working in an Ebola treatment clinic in Sierra Leone, tested negative for the Ebola virus after developing flu-like symptoms and being isolated at a Sydney hospital. Dr. Parker had been working in West Africa since November and had followed protocol by notifying authorities upon returning to Australia. NSW Health confirmed the results, stating that no further testing for Ebola was required.

A schoolboy named Frankie Franz, inspired by Barcelona's Martin Montoya, successfully replicated a 27-yard goal into a basketball hoop, surprising both his teammates and family. After watching Montoya perform the trick shot, Frankie attempted the feat himself in his garden and managed to score on his first try, impressing his mother with the accuracy and power of his kick. Frankie, who dreams of playing for top clubs like Real Madrid or Barcelona, demonstrated remarkable skill and confidence in executing the challenging shot.

The Wisden–MCC Cricket Photograph of the Year 2014 short-list features stunning images capturing the global appeal of cricket, from professional athletes like Dwayne Bravo making spectacular catches to amateur players in unique settings such as on a rubbish tip in Bangladesh or on the summit of Mount Kilimanjaro. Notably, the winning photograph by Matthew Lewis showcases Bravo's extraordinary full-length catch during the ICC World Twenty20. The collection also includes poignant moments such as Joe Russell's failed attempt at a catch and the tragic scene of Australian batsman Phillip Hughes walking to the changing rooms after being fatally struck by a ball.

In a custody dispute, a New Jersey judge dismissed a father's claim that his ex-wife abused her parental discretion by taking their 11-year-old daughter to see Pink's concert, ruling that the performances were not sexually inappropriate for a preteen. The judge, after considering the mother's reasons and speaking with the child, found no evidence of bad parenting and stated that the girl had a positive experience. The judge also noted that Pink's work, while sometimes suggestive, is not inherently inappropriate for young audiences.

Salcombe, a coastal town in Devon, has surpassed London as the most expensive place to buy property in the UK, with the average property costing £671,759. This surge in property values has also driven up the cost of waterfront properties to over £2 million, surpassing some of London's priciest areas such as Notting Hill and Regent's Park. As a result, Salcombe is becoming an increasingly popular destination for summer holidays, offering luxury accommodations like the Salcombe Harbour Hotel & Spa, where waterfront rooms are available for around £425 during the summer season.

Celtic Football Club has criticized the Scottish Football Association (SFA) over the ticket prices for their Scottish Cup semi-final against Inverness Caledonian Thistle at Hampden Park. Celtic argue that the North Stand tickets, priced at £23, are too expensive compared to other areas of the stadium, particularly given the expected high demand from Celtic supporters. The SFA defended its decision, stating that all participating clubs were consulted, ticket prices had remained unchanged for four years, and revenues from the matches were distributed evenly among the teams.

A 16-year-old student named Rebecca Rice was allowed to bring her pet Labrador, Holly, into a GCSE French oral exam to help calm her nerves, as nothing else had worked previously. The school’s French teacher, Lorette Esteve, supported this decision after seeing Rebecca's struggles and suggested the presence of her dog. This unique arrangement proved successful, with Rebecca stating that having Holly by her side significantly reduced her anxiety during the five-minute test.

Anders Lindegaard, a goalkeeper for Manchester United who has struggled for playing time, took advantage of the English weather to enjoy a day off with his wife Misse Beqiri. Lindegaard, who has been with Beqiri since 2012 and married in a beach ceremony in Mauritius, shared the moment on Instagram, highlighting their relationship even as he faces challenges in his football career. Despite being third-choice goalkeeper, Lindegaard's personal life remains a source of happiness and positivity.

Spanish goalkeepers David de Gea and Victor Valdes took advantage of the sunny weather by visiting a theme park, following Manchester United's recent impressive victory over Manchester City. This comes as the team has shown strong form in the latter part of the season, competing for a top-four finish in the Premier League. However, the article also hints at uncertainties regarding their future at the club, as Valdes has struggled for playing time and both players' contracts may not be renewed.

A 75-year-old piano teacher, John Goodwin, shot himself outside a New Hampshire courthouse while awaiting a jury's verdict on six charges of aggravated felonious sexual assault. The former student, now 24, testified that he did not report the alleged assaults for years due to embarrassment, but Goodwin's lawyer maintained that his client was merely "touchy-feely" and did not commit a crime. Goodwin was taken to the hospital with life-threatening injuries but his health status was not immediately disclosed.

Amazon removed "Rescue the Anorexia Girl," a controversial computer game that encouraged players to feed a cartoon anorexic character, after receiving numerous complaints. The game, marketed as a way to combat anorexia, featured players throwing food at the character to prevent her from losing weight and dying, but was widely criticized for potentially stigmatizing those with eating disorders. Critics argued that the game trivialized a serious medical condition and could discourage individuals from seeking help.

Scientists are working to digitally recreate the cognitive abilities of the honeybee to develop a robot that mimics its thinking, sensing, and acting capabilities. This project, known as the Green Brain Project, involves mapping the bee's brain and creating digital circuits that mimic its functions, allowing a drone to fly like a bee. While the project has successfully cloned the bee's vision processing, the ultimate goal is to create a versatile robotic system capable of tasks such as crop pollination and search and rescue missions.

A newlywed couple from Air Malta recently took a romantic flight over the Mediterranean, with their passenger jet flying in the shape of two giant hearts shortly after takeoff. This unusual flight path was to celebrate the marriage of one of the pilots to a cabin crew member, with the couple and their family and friends taking a short sight-seeing tour over the Mediterranean. The special flight was noted on the arrivals' board at Malta International Airport with the status 'Just Married', and while some saw it as a creative training flight, others speculated it was a PR stunt or marriage proposal.

At Kristiansand Zoo in Norway, a tragic incident occurred on Easter Monday where Melvin, a five-year-old giraffe, died after being gored by an eland antelope while his head was stuck in the enclosure's fence. The attack, which took place in front of around 30 witnesses including children, was unprovoked, and despite efforts by veterinarians, the giraffe could not be saved. Melvin, a popular attraction at the zoo since his birth in 2010, had been named in a local newspaper competition.

A restaurant manager in Leuven, Belgium, sparked outrage after charging a mother 36p for heating up her baby's feeding bottle, prompting her to share the bill on Twitter. The incident drew widespread criticism, with many users calling the manager "the stingiest boss in Europe." The Horeca Vlaanderen restaurant chain later clarified that such charges are uncommon in most establishments and would only apply if explicitly stated to customers beforehand.

North Korea accused Mexico of illegally detaining one of its cargo ships, the Mu Du Bong, which had run aground off Mexico's coast in July. Mexico defended the detention, citing that the ship's owner had violated United Nations sanctions. North Korea denied the charges, claiming the ship was innocent and that the crew should be released.

Prime Minister David Cameron is set to announce plans to provide an additional 600,000 free childcare places for children aged 3 to 4, aiming to reduce the financial burden on parents and increase employment opportunities. These measures include doubling the existing 15-hour free childcare provision to 30 hours per week, valued at £5,000 annually for working families. The Conservative Party justifies these initiatives as part of their broader strategy to reward hard work and reduce poverty through increased employment.

Manchester City secured their place in the FA Youth Cup final by scoring two late goals against Leicester City, extending their lead from the first leg to 5-1 on aggregate. The goals came from substitutes Isaac Buckley and Brandon Barker, while Layton Ndukwu had briefly given Leicester hope with a penalty. Manchester City will face Chelsea in the final at either the City Football Academy Stadium or Stamford Bridge on April 20 and 27, respectively.

During a nationally broadcast Q&A session, Russian President Vladimir Putin dismissed the impact of Western sanctions, predicting they would not end soon, and defended the sale of a sophisticated air defense system to Iran, despite concerns from Israel and the West. The session, which attracted 2.4 million questions, allowed Putin to engage with the public in a rare, live, and extended format, though critics view it as a staged event rather than a genuine opportunity for dialogue. Putin also addressed the presence of NSA whistleblower Edward Snowden, who questioned the president about Moscow's surveillance practices via video link.

Gary Gardner, a 22-year-old midfielder who previously had a successful loan spell at Nottingham Forest, is set to return to Aston Villa for pre-season training to be evaluated by new manager Tim Sherwood.
